Cystitis Signs and symptoms of cystitis (inflammation of the blad- der) include suprapubic pain, dysuria, frequency and ur- gency of urination, nocturia, and haematuria. It may have various causes but is usually associated with urinary-tract infections (see p.199). Non-infectious cystitis can occur as an adverse effect of some drugs such as NSAIDs (notably tiaprofenic acid).1 Pelvic radiotherapy and some drugs used for cancer chemotherapy can also cause haemorrhag- ic cystitis (below). Other inflammatory non-infectious forms of cystitis include interstitial cystitis (see below) and rare conditions such as eosinophilic cystitis.2 1. Bramble FJ, Morley R.
